2610.06360.title: Ontology Concept Overlap as a Training Signal: Knowledge-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Clinical Question Answering
2610.06360.paper_summary: Reinforcement learning post-training for language models relies on two reward designs: human preferences (RLHF, DPO) and binary verifiers (RLVR). Clinical question answering fits neither. Near-correct answers differ by a single substituted entity, and no executable check decides clinical correctness. We instantiate a soft verifier from a maintained controlled vocabulary: UMLS Concept Unique Identifier overlap (via scispaCy, set-level F1) gives a graded, externally specified reward computed without a model in the loop. We combine it inside GRPO with an entropy-normalised LLM judge, which covers the safety and evidence axes overlap cannot see, and a small consistency penalty on padding and repetition that keeps early-training samples scorable. This three-term composite improves over SFT on Phi-3-mini (3.8B) over MedQA by 2.9% on EM (0.700 vs 0.680) and 39% on Token-F1 (0.202 vs 0.145); on Llama-3.2-3B the corresponding gains are 14% on EM and 35% on Token-F1. We report Token-F1 as the primary metric because it credits partially-correct clinical content that EM discards at this open-generation scale. Main-table results are means over 3 seeds with standard deviations below 0.005. The method transfers to PubMedQA, where training on the PubMedQA train set with the same composite reward improves Token-F1 over SFT by 22% on Phi-3-mini and 17% on Llama-3.2-3B without retuning. A reward ablation on Phi-3, varying the judge-ontology split at a fixed consistency weight, attributes 3 EM points to the ontology term, the contribution that catches entity substitutions the judge cannot. Three negative findings constrain the design: DPO under random negatives underperforms SFT for strong-prior models but helps the weakest-prior one; PPO under a sparse neural reward diverges; GRPO with KL-in-loss collapses at 7B.
2610.06360.paper_summary_zh: 強化學習後訓練語言模型依賴於兩種獎勵設計：人類偏好（RLHF, DPO）和二元驗證器（RLVR）。臨床問題回答不符合這兩者。接近正確的答案僅因一個替換的實體而異，且沒有可執行的檢查來決定臨床正確性。我們從維護的受控詞彙中實現了一個軟驗證器：UMLS 概念唯一標識符重疊（通過 scispaCy，集合級 F1）提供了一個分級的、外部指定的獎勵，計算時不需要模型參與。我們將其與熵正規化的 LLM 評判者結合在 GRPO 中，該評判者涵蓋了安全性和證據軸的重疊，這是無法通過其他方式看到的，並且對填充和重複施加了一個小的一致性懲罰，以保持早期訓練樣本的可評分性。這個三項合成在 Phi-3-mini（3.8B）上相對於 MedQA 的 SFT 提升了 2.9% 的 EM（0.700 對 0.680）和 39% 的 Token-F1（0.202 對 0.145）；在 Llama-3.2-3B 上，對應的增益分別為 EM 的 14% 和 Token-F1 的 35%。我們報告 Token-F1 作為主要指標，因為它對部分正確的臨床內容給予了信用，而 EM 在這個開放生成的範疇中則會丟棄這些內容。主表結果是基於 3 個種子的均值，標準差低於 0.005。該方法可轉移到 PubMedQA，對 PubMedQA 訓練集進行相同合成獎勵的訓練，Token-F1 在 Phi-3-mini 上相對於 SFT 提升了 22%，在 Llama-3.2-3B 上提升了 17%，且不需要重新調整。對 Phi-3 的獎勵消融，變化評判者-本體的分割在固定的一致性權重下，將 3 EM 點歸因於本體術語，這一貢獻捕捉了評判者無法識別的實體替換。三個負面發現限制了設計：在隨機負例下 DPO 表現不如 SFT 對於強先驗模型，但對於最弱的先驗模型有幫助；在稀疏神經獎勵下 PPO 發散；GRPO 與 KL-in-loss 在 7B 時崩潰。
